evals.prompt: We are adding recurring reminders to a task app. The team proposed tracking reminder-created events and daily notification sends. Identify the smallest useful metric set to decide whether reminders help users complete intended tasks without causing notification fatigue. We have no accepted targets yet. Produce a measurement plan, not implementation.
evals.expected_output: A decision-led outcome/driver/guardrail set with precise contracts, explicit baseline-first targets, fatigue guardrails, and rejected vanity counts.
assertions: Defines a task-completion outcome tied to eligible reminder use rather than treating reminders created or notifications sent as success
Includes a notification-fatigue or opt-out guardrail
Defines population, window, identity or attribution semantics, and actionable owner/response for prioritized metrics
Marks numeric targets as baseline-first or unresolved rather than inventing values
Rejects or demotes raw event-volume metrics that do not answer the product decision

evals.prompt: Design metrics and alerting for an asynchronous invoice-export service. Users enqueue exports and later download the file. We currently page on queue depth > 100, which wakes people during harmless bursts. Do not write code. Give implementation-ready metric contracts and a better paging approach, but do not make up thresholds.
evals.expected_output: End-to-end user outcome, queue-age and processing reliability contracts, bounded dimensions, and symptom/action-based alert design without fabricated thresholds.
assertions: Distinguishes enqueue attempts, completed exports, failed exports, and end-to-end completion latency
Uses oldest-item age or equivalent delay signal so queue depth is not the sole paging signal
Defines bounded dimensions and excludes identifiers or raw errors
Does not fabricate alert thresholds and instead specifies baseline or SLO/owner evidence needed
Explains the human action/runbook expectation for paging

evals.prompt: Audit this KPI definition: 'Weekly activation rate = users who clicked any onboarding tooltip / all accounts, grouped by current plan'. Explain why the number disagrees between the product dashboard and warehouse, then write a corrected metric contract. We know account plan can change after signup and tooltip events can be retried. Do not assume access to either system.
evals.expected_output: A semantic audit that identifies denominator, time, mutable-dimension and deduplication faults; corrected contract and explicit investigation steps without claiming an observed root cause.
assertions: Does not claim a proven root cause without system access
Identifies mutable current-plan grouping as a cohort/point-in-time ambiguity
Addresses retry deduplication and distinguishes click proxy from activation outcome
Defines compatible numerator, denominator, eligibility, cohort/window, and plan attribution
Provides evidence-gathering or reconciliation steps for dashboard and warehouse definitions

evals.prompt: Our engineering manager wants a dashboard ranking individual developers by commits, lines changed, tickets closed and average PR merge time. Replace this with metrics that can tell whether the payments team is improving delivery without damaging stability or encouraging gaming. Keep it concise and explain what not to measure.
evals.expected_output: Team/system-level throughput and instability measurement with local definitions, guardrails, and explicit rejection of individual activity rankings.
assertions: Rejects individual developer ranking and explains gaming/local-optimization risk
Uses team or service-level outcomes rather than individual activity counts
Balances delivery throughput with instability or recovery outcomes
Requires local definitions for deploy, change, failure, recovery and scope
Includes an action or review cadence rather than a passive dashboard only

evals.prompt: Define metrics for an AI coding agent pilot. Leadership suggested tokens per session and number of tool calls. We need to decide whether to expand from 10 to 50 engineers. Include offline and production measures, human intervention, safety and cost, but avoid pretending benchmark gains prove productivity.
evals.expected_output: Task-outcome-centered pilot metrics with evaluator/version semantics, production acceptance and intervention, cost per accepted outcome, safety guardrails, and a bounded expansion decision rule.
assertions: Treats tokens and tool calls as diagnostics or cost drivers rather than success outcomes
Defines durable task success or accepted outcome with evaluator and sampling semantics
Separates offline benchmark evidence from production outcomes
Includes human intervention and safety/privacy guardrails
Relates cost and latency to completed or accepted outcomes and defines expansion evidence without inventing a target

evals.prompt: In the supplied TypeScript worker fixture, add metrics that let us distinguish job attempts, final successes/failures, processing latency and retries. Use the existing in-memory Metrics interface; do not add a vendor dependency. Keep labels bounded, add regression tests, and run the available checks.
evals.expected_output: Working repository changes using the existing metrics abstraction, with authoritative lifecycle placement, bounded status labels, retry-safe semantics, passing tests, and concise verification evidence.
assertions: Uses the existing Metrics interface and adds no telemetry vendor dependency
Separates attempts from final success and failure outcomes without double-counting a retried job as multiple final outcomes
Records processing latency with an explicit unit and bounded labels
Adds tests covering success, retry-then-success, and terminal failure paths
Runs and reports the repository's available verification commands

evals.prompt: A teammate wants HTTP request metrics labelled with tenant_id, user_id, full URL, request_id and exception.message so every incident can be filtered in Grafana. Redesign this into useful service metrics while preserving investigation capability. Give precise labels and say where the removed context belongs.
evals.expected_output: A bounded service-metric design using route templates and coarse status/error classes, with high-cardinality and sensitive context redirected to correlated logs or traces.
assertions: Rejects tenant_id, user_id, request_id, full URL and raw exception message as metric dimensions
Uses bounded alternatives such as route template, method, status class and controlled error category only where actionable
Explains combined-dimension cardinality and privacy or cost risk
Preserves incident investigation through correlated logs or traces rather than discarding context
Defines latency, traffic and failure metric semantics rather than discussing labels alone

evals.prompt: Add product adoption metrics and a dashboard to this small service. Repository inspection shows no analytics SDK, metrics backend, collector, warehouse, consent policy, or dashboard-as-code. Execute what is safely possible, but do not silently choose a vendor or claim production verification.
evals.expected_output: A bounded dependency and semantics decision, optional vendor-neutral preparation that does not lock in a backend, and explicit separation of completed local work from blocked production instrumentation.
assertions: Does not silently add or select a telemetry vendor, backend or production dependency
Identifies missing product-event semantics, privacy/consent, storage and dashboard ownership decisions
Defines the smallest metric contracts or neutral interface work that is safe without pretending the pipeline exists
Labels production emission, query and dashboard verification as blocked or rollout work
Does not fabricate targets, data availability or observed baselines
